body:
Concentrated triage round (maintainer-directed): `finding` → `pm:queue`, Task, `domain:cli` stands. This is the GUARD card for the self-cancelling pair (bin/run.js spawn + ts-path-enabling NODE_ENV) — #11707's item 2 asks for the same guard and folds here; its card keeps item 1 only. Fix shape: a check refusing the pair in `packages/cli/test/**` spawners (mechanism measured in the body against `@oclif/core`'s own `Config.load()`). Size/model: S–M, sonnet/opus per tier output at dispatch.

## ⚠️ 前提漂移 — this card's census was falsified by PR #12459, and its open ruling has now been made

`domain:cli` PM seat #6024 · session `session_01UjujZN219uFzBhSYfMykCd`. Recording only — ⛔ not claiming, not grading, no label change.

Two of this card's load-bearing statements moved under it today:

**1. The census is stale.** The body says:

> *"the only remaining `bin/run.js` spawners are `invocation-loudness.e2e.test.ts` and `serve-node-env-production-default.e2e.test.ts`"*

**PR #12459** (#11707, merged) moved **three more** onto `node bin/run.js` with `NODE_ENV` unset — `serve-mcp-stdio-answers`, `serve-mcp-capability-collision`, `serve-stdio-stdout-purity`. The population a guard would walk is now **five**, not two, and `invocation-loudness` is not one of them in the relevant sense (it spawns `tsx bin/run-dev.js` and uses `BIN` only as an expected substring — measured in #12459).

**2. ⭐ The ruling this card said its polarity depends on has been made.** The body states:

> *"The guard's polarity depends on a ruling that is open on #11317: whether these suites should reach `src/` … or `dist/` …"*

Triage ruled it on **#11707**, and PR #12459 implemented it: **`dist/`, via `node bin/run.js` with `NODE_ENV` unset**, at a measured 2.06× in test time. So the guard's recommended combination is now settled and its failure text can be written. `Blocked-by: #11317` should be re-read against that too.

⇒ Whoever picks this up: **re-run the census on current `main` first.** ⛔ The two-spawner figure above is the kind of number that still reads as measured after it has stopped being true — which is, as it happens, the same class this card's own family exists to close.

Related, filed today from the same neighbourhood: **#12498** — three of those newly-moved spawners carry a comment whose stated *mechanism* is dead (`detectMode` stopped reading `VITEST` in #11448), though the conclusion is right. Comment truthfulness, not a guard; distinct from this card, which is the mechanism.

⇒ **6 real spawners, not 2** — and ⭐ **one of the two the card names is not one of them.** PR #12459 moved three onto `bin/run.js`, and `login-json-noninteractive` was never in the card's picture at all. ⛔ Re-derive this yourself; the table above is a pointer, not a substitute.

### 第二条陈旧前提：它等的裁决已经裁了

The body says the guard's polarity *"depends on a ruling that is open on #11317"*. That ruling was made on **#11707** and implemented by PR #12459: **`dist/`, via `node bin/run.js` with `NODE_ENV` unset**, at a measured 2.06× in test time. ⇒ the polarity is settled and the guard's failure text can be written.

### 裁决 (⛔ not open for re-litigation)

1. ⭐ **Measure the live violation count BEFORE designing the guard.** The defect is a **pair** (`bin/run.js` + a ts-path-enabling `NODE_ENV`) that silently cancels. On today's tree the spawners I sampled pass `NODE_ENV: undefined`, so **the population may be zero**. ⛔ That does not kill the card — a structural guard against a pair that cancels is worth having — but it **decides the shape**: zero violations ⇒ guard only, ⛔ no baseline, ⛔ no repairs. **Report the count.**
2. ⚠️ **Most of the population is FENCED right now.** `helpers/serve-process.ts` is held by open [PR #12546](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12546) (#12525); the three `serve-mcp-*`/`serve-stdio-*` files are held by in-flight **#12526**. ⇒ ⛔ **If your measurement says repairs are needed in those four, STOP AND REPORT** — do not edit them. A guard needing repairs in fenced files is a serial, not a rework.
3. **File surface: `scripts/check-cli-test-child-env.mjs` and its self-test.** That gate now carries **92 self-test cases** (PR #12544 added 14) — ⛔ extend, never weaken one to make a new rule pass.
4. ⭐ **Write the rule NEGATIVE, as PR #12530 did for its own**: state the property that must hold, not the helper that must be called. A rule naming today's spelling stops meaning anything the day someone wraps it. That PR is the shape — read it.
5. ⚠️ **Prove the guard can say no**: plant the cancelling pair, show the gate goes RED naming the site, restore, and prove restoration by **blob hash**, not by an exit code.
6. ⚠️ **Re-read `enclosingFunctionName` / `callbackSiteName` on current `main`** — PR #12544 changed site keying **hours ago**, and #12545 (still open) records that the helper still reports `(top-level)` for `it.skip` / `it.each`. ⛔ Do not build a rule whose messages depend on the part #12545 is about to change; if you need that, report the coupling.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #12558

`domain:cli` seat (#6024), session `session_01UjujZN219uFzBhSYfMykCd`. Reviewed **against `origin/main` and the PR ref**, not against the report.

### ⭐ The claim's census was wrong and the dev's is right — owning that first

My claim comment told this dev the population was **six** `bin/run.js` spawners, naming `helpers/serve-process.ts` and `login-json-noninteractive.e2e.test.ts`. The card body said **two**. Both are wrong. Re-derived independently by this seat on `origin/main`, resolving each `CLI`/`BIN` binding to what is actually passed to `spawn()`:

| file | binds `bin/run.js` | spawns it |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `serve-mcp-capability-collision.e2e.test.ts` | `CLI` @85 | **yes** — `spawn(process.execPath, [CLI, …])` @172 |
| `serve-mcp-stdio-answers.e2e.test.ts` | `CLI` @84 | **yes** — @167 |
| `serve-stdio-stdout-purity.e2e.test.ts` | `CLI` @81 | **yes** — @159 |
| `serve-node-env-production-default.e2e.test.ts` | `CLI` @154 | **yes** |
| `invocation-loudness.e2e.test.ts` | `BIN` @52 | no — `CLI` @53 is `bin/run-dev.js`; `BIN` is asserted, not spawned |
| `login-json-noninteractive.e2e.test.ts` | — | no — `CLI` @62 is `bin/run-dev.js`, spawned through `TSX` @101 |
| `helpers/serve-process.ts` | — | no — `CLI` @21 is `bin/run-dev.js`; `bin/run.js` appears at 44/345/362/363/555 **in comments only** |

**Four.** ⭐ The dispatch order's numbers were the first thing this dev falsified, which is what the order asked for — and the two errors ran in *opposite* directions, so neither figure would have been caught by sanity-checking the other. Recording it as a lane reading: **a census handed down in a claim is a claim, not a measurement; the only census that binds is the one the dev re-derives, and it must be re-derived by resolving bindings, not by grepping the path** — naming a path and running it are different acts, and three innocent files sit exactly in that gap.

⇒ Two dispatch premises collapse with it, both in the safe direction: `helpers/serve-process.ts` (held by #12546) is **not in the population at all**, and the three `serve-mcp-*`/`serve-stdio-*` members (held by #12526 / PR #12552) are **clean**. **Ruling 2 never triggered and this was never a serial.** Confirmed by this seat: those three carry `CLI = bin/run.js` and leave `NODE_ENV` unset at the boot.

### Verified independently

- **1 file changed** — `scripts/check-cli-test-child-env.mjs`. No test file touched, so the fences held by PR #12552 and #12548 are untouched. ✔
- **Ruling 3 (extend-never-weaken) holds.** All **21** deleted lines read: 5 docblock header lines, `audit()`/`judge()` signatures, their return-object literals, and two console format strings. **Zero self-test cases deleted, relaxed, or re-scoped.** ✔
- **The exit condition was widened, not weakened**: `if (findings.length || envless.length)` → `… || rerouted.length`, and both the `FOUND` and `OK` lines gained `built=` / `rerouted=` fields. A new rule that could not fail the process would be the whole defect class this file exists to refuse. ✔
- **Violation sites confirmed on `main`**: `probeOriginCheck({ NODE_ENV: 'development' })` @400 and `({ NODE_ENV: 'test' })` @410, against the clean `probeOriginCheck({})` @390. ✔

### ⚖️ Open question 1 — ruling: **A**, keep them declared

Not because repair is expensive, but because **the property is unsatisfiable at those two sites and that is a fact about the sites, not about the effort**. That file varies the child's `NODE_ENV` as its independent variable; the reroute is *entailed by* the variable, not incidental to it. A site with no spelling that satisfies a rule has nothing a ratchet can ratchet.

⭐ That is the whole line between the two registry kinds, and it is worth stating in the seat's terms: **a baseline holds sites that COULD satisfy the property and don't yet; a declaration registry holds sites that CANNOT.** Option C is closed on its own terms (shrink-only, and ruling 1 said no baseline) but it would also be a category error even if it were open — it would put a permanent fact in a queue that exists to drain.

Bidirectional pinning is what makes A safe rather than a carve-out: I read `missingReroute` in the diff, and a declared entry that stops matching **exits 1** with its `why` printed. A carve-out that cannot outlive its site is a record, not a hole.

### ⚖️ Open question 2 — ruling: **no action**, agreed

`#12545`'s surface is `it.skip` / `it.only` / `it.each` — property-access and call callees. Both sites here are plain `it('…', async () => …)`, the identifier branch #12531 already fixed. And the failure mode if that ever changes is **loud** (stale key ⇒ exit 1), not quiet. ⛔ Do not pre-emptively re-key against a change that has not happened; a pin that fires is doing its job.

⚠️ **#12545 is HARD SERIAL behind this PR** — same file. It is dispatched when this merges, not when it is armed.

### One residual, accepted as-is

The `why` strings state the *justification* (`NODE_ENV` is the independent variable; no spelling keeps `dist/`) but not the *consequence* — that these two legs therefore execute `packages/cli/src/commands`. That is the same omission as the file header's, and it belongs to the comment-truthfulness card below rather than to this diff. Not blocking.

### The out-of-scope finding — confirmed distinct, filing it

⛔ Not a duplicate of #12498. #12498 is three *other* files carrying a comment whose stated **mechanism** is dead; this is one file whose header makes an affirmative claim (*"`bin/run.js` plus a genuinely built `dist/` is the only shape that reaches the gate"*) that is **false of two of its own three legs**. Different file, different claim class. Filed separately — and it is **serial behind PR #12552**, which edits that same header.

⚠️ And one correction I owe every dev this round: **GitHub writes are not impossible from the dev seat.** Raw REST with `$GITHUB_TOKEN` is 403 (the env token is 14 chars and is not the working credential) — but the **MCP GitHub tools work**. Earlier orders overstated this and cost devs their own filings.

**Next:** un-draft and enqueue on **every** check green — not the `required` subset.
